title: Your rights and how to use them
intro: The General Data Protection Regulation gives you control over your personal data. This page explains each right in plain terms and the quickest way to use it with Vibed. Our [Privacy Policy](/privacy) describes the processing itself.

head: You want to
How
rows: See or download your style profile
Delete a project and its files
Delete your account and all its data
Stop the weekly summary and product updates
The unsubscribe link at the bottom of those emails
Accept or refuse the error replay
Cookie settings, in the footer of the home page or on the [Cookie Policy](/cookie-policy)
Anything else (copy of your data, correction, objection...)

defs.desc: Know whether we process your data and get a copy of it, with the purposes, recipients and retention periods.
Have inaccurate or incomplete data corrected.
Have your data deleted, unless we must keep it by law (billing records, for example).
Ask us to pause the use of your data while a dispute about it is examined.
Object to processing based on our legitimate interest, such as your style profile or product emails. For product emails, objection is always granted.
Receive the data you provided, in a structured and machine-readable format, or have it sent to another service where technically possible.
Withdraw your consent at any time. This does not affect what was done before.
Give instructions on how your data should be kept, deleted or passed on after your death (French Data Protection Act, article 85).

sections.title: How we handle a request
blocks: Send your request from the email address linked to your account if you can, so we can match it quickly. We answer within one month. For complex requests, this can be extended by two more months, in which case we tell you why within the first month. Requests are free, unless they are clearly unfounded or excessive.
We only ask for proof of identity when we have a reasonable doubt that the request comes from you.

sections.title: Complaints
blocks: If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can lodge a complaint with the CNIL (Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés), 3 place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07, or online at [www.cnil.fr](https://www.cnil.fr). If you live in another EU country, you can also contact the authority of that country.
